turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want to practise joining sentences. I find it difficult.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Joining sentences is a good thing to practise.

Do you know the word "and"? We use "and" to join two ideas in one sentence.

Example: I like tea and I like milk.

Now you try. Join these two sentences with "and":

I have a cat. I have a dog.

turns.learner: I have a cat and I have a dog.
turns.tutor:
Yes, "I have a cat and I have a dog." is correct. You used "and" to join two ideas in one sentence. Well done!

Here is the exercise as written:

Join with and: "I have a cat. I have a dog."

turns.learner: I did this one already, teacher. Can I try another sentence?
turns.tutor:
You are right, sorry. You already did that one well.

Now let's try a new joining word: "but". We use "but" when two ideas are different from each other.

Join with but: "The bus is cheap. It is slow."

turns.learner: The bus is cheap. But it is slow.
turns.tutor:
Good, you used "but" to show a contrast. One small point: "but" joins the two ideas inside one sentence, so we do not put a full stop before it.

Now a new one, with "because". We use "because" to give a reason.

Join with because: "I am happy. It is my birthday."

turns.learner: I am happy. Because it is my birthday.
turns.tutor:
Good, your reason is right: "it is my birthday". Small point: no full stop before "because".

Quick recap:
"but" shows a contrast, and "because" gives a reason, in the same sentence.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: We use and, but, because to join two sentences. Because gives the reason. I think after the full stop is okay.
turns.tutor:
You are right that "because" gives a reason. But the full stop part is not correct.

A linking word joins two ideas in one sentence, so there is no full stop before it.

Right: I stayed home because I was sick.
Wrong: I stayed home. Because I was sick.

Please say the rule again, with the full stop part.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: Oh, I see. So no full stop before because. We write it all in one sentence with the two ideas.
turns.tutor:
Remember: a linking word joins two ideas in one sentence, with no full stop before it.

Now try one on your own. Write one sentence about yourself with "because". Say what you like or do not like, and give a reason.

Tell me the rule in your own words.
